text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Jackie Robinson was born on January 31, 1919, in Cairo, Georgia, to a family of sharecroppers. [D]
On April 15, 1947, he played his first major league game for the Brooklyn Dodgers, ending more than sixty years of segregation in major league baseball. [D]
His retirement from baseball was announced in January 1957; he then worked in business and as a spokesman and fundraiser for civil rights causes, including the NAACP. [D]
He was diagnosed with diabetes at about 37, around the time he retired from baseball, and at first kept it private; two of his brothers also had diabetes. [D]
By 1969, at 50, he had nerve and artery damage in his legs. [D]
In 1970 he had two mild strokes. [D]
His eldest son, Jackie Robinson Jr., was killed in an automobile accident on June 17, 1971, at 24. [D]

text.paragraph: 6 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

Urgent retina consultation within 48 hours for blurred vision with new floaters in a man with long-standing diabetes: dilated examination, OCT, and treatment of any proliferative retinopathy or macular edema; same-day attendance for a curtain over the vision or flashes. Guideline: 12. Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); Diabetic Retinopathy Preferred Practice Pattern (2025) [S]

Glucose: continue metformin and basal insulin, titrated slowly by a written plan so that the A1c falls gradually; rescue glucagon; diabetes self-management education adapted for low vision (a talking glucose meter, an insulin pen with audible dose clicks, large-print plans). Guideline: 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); 9. Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes type 2, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, ischemic heart disease, chronic kidney disease and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Cardiovascular risk: atorvastatin increased to 80 mg, aspirin continued, baseline ECG; cardiology evaluation of exertional chest tightness with a pharmacologic stress test, since calf pain limits walking. Guideline: 10. Cardiovascular Disease and Risk Management: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes type 2, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, ischemic heart disease, chronic kidney disease and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Legs and feet: comprehensive foot examination today; ankle-brachial index; daily foot checks with a magnifying mirror and a bright lamp, protective shoes; podiatry. Guideline: 12. Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); 2024 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/APMA/ABC/SCAI/SVM/SVN/SVS/SIR/VESS Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease (2024) [S]

Kidneys: repeat urine albumin and kidney function after any change in kidney medicines; no NSAIDs. Guideline: 11. Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024) [S]

Grief and mood: acknowledge the loss, PHQ-9 now and at three months, and an offer of the health center's grief counselor, which he accepted; call or text 988 if thoughts of self-harm ever arise. Guideline: 5. Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026 (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes type 2, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, ischemic heart disease, chronic kidney disease and depression monographs (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
